transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Lately I keep thinking about death, and I’m starting to worry about the thoughts I’m having about not wanting to be here anymore. It's really starting to scare me, which is why I knew I needed to come in and get some help.
Have you had any thoughts about how you would act on these feelings, or have you made any plans?

I don't have a concrete, active plan, but I've spent a lot of time online reading about painless ways to die and methods of self-harm, and I've found myself picturing doing it. It deeply frightens me because it feels so much more intense than just a passing thought.
Have you felt this way before, or is this the first time you've experienced such intense thoughts and low mood?
No, I've never experienced anything this severe before. This is the first time I've ever felt this way, and it is honestly really new and frightening for me.
In addition to thoughts of death, have you been feeling down, sad, or lost interest in activities most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes, for about three weeks now—ever since I found out I failed my certification exam—I've been waking up almost every day with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like painting and salsa dancing, and I just end up canceling on my friends to sit on the couch.
Besides losing interest in painting and dancing, have you also noticed a lack of pleasure in other activities you used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or eating your favorite foods?

Yes, I've been dodging calls and canceling on my friends because I just don't have the energy to show up for anyone anymore. My appetite is also completely gone, and even when my mom drops off my favorite homemade food, it just sits in the fridge because everything tastes like cardboard.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, such as waking up very early and not being able to go back to sleep, or sleeping too much?
I haven't really noticed any major sleep issues like waking up too early or sleeping too much. The only thing is that I sometimes just fall asleep on the couch out of pure exhaustion.
Have you noticed feeling emotionally numb or unable to feel joy, even in moments that used to make you happy?

Yes, I feel completely numb and hollow inside, and I just can't experience joy anymore. Things I used to love, like painting after a shift or going to salsa nights with my friends, now feel so exhausting and pointless that I just cancel on everyone and isolate myself. It feels like nothing can bring me happiness right now.
Have you also noticed a significant decrease in your ability to feel pleasure in activities you once enjoyed, even in small moments like seeing a friend or eating something tasty?

Yes, definitely. Even the thought of painting or going to salsa nights with my friends feels completely exhausting and pointless, so I just cancel on them. Food has also lost all its appeal, and even my mom's homemade food just sits in the fridge because everything tastes like cardboard.
Over the past few weeks, have you also felt slowed down physically or had trouble concentrating on simple tasks like reading or making decisions?

Yes, physically I feel like I'm wading through mud, and my coworkers have actually noticed me moving slowly and taking a long time to answer simple questions. Mentally, my brain is so foggy that I can't absorb anything from my study guides, I lose track of what patients are telling me, and I get completely frozen just trying to decide what to wear to work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-episode major depressive episode characterized by persistent depressed mood, markedly diminished interest and pleasure (anhedonia), significant weight/appetite loss, psychomotor retardation, fatigue, impaired concentration, and recurrent thoughts of death with passive suicidal ideation. Symptoms have been present nearly every day for the past three weeks, causing clinically significant functional impairment. No prior depressive episodes are reported, ruling out recurrent depression. The severity is severe based on the intensity of symptoms and suicidal ideation, though without a concrete plan.
